Quotech understands the mundane tasks which consume the precious time of underwriters and brokers. Every Quotech platform is custom built to give this time back. Unsurpassed solutions. Quotech creates and delivers hand-made underwriting and broking platforms, designed by a veteran of Lloyd’s and the London company market, to surpass your commercial insurance needs precisely, end to end. Unbending clarity. Quotech platforms constantly compile and sift the data to give everyone exactly the information they need, in just the right place, while storing everything in a unique Corporate Data Treasury to provide a single source of truth. Unmatched functionality. Quotech believes very much in having all the bells and whistles (provided they’re useful), so Quotech platforms automate ALL the mundane tasks, creating room for users to practise the twin arts of underwriting and broking. Unbeaten connectivity. Whatever you need to link and mesh with other systems, internal or external, Quotech has it covered, from powerful APIs that link systems seamlessly, to built-in Lloyd’s risk codes, underwriting authorities, automated bordereaux compilation, and instant document delivery. Uncomplicated interfaces. Quotech builds simple, intuitive front ends which present the functionality and organise the details, even down to user level, while hiding the complexity of data in the background. Uncompromising understanding. Quotech makes systems from scratch to eliminate the specific process pinch-points and time-wasters that individual customers endure, so every build begins with extensive discovery – especially including consultation with future users – to be sure they are understood. ​ Our Customers. Our Big Story Quotech’s story began in 2020, when principal Guillaume Bonnissent was a Chief Underwriting Officer at a large London-market MGA. He tried to buy-in an IT platform to organise the firm’s data and make it available, selectively and usefully, to his underwriters and others. No such platform was on offer, so Guillaume – who’s no stranger to writing computer code – decided to build one himself. To learn what happened next, read Quotech’s Big Story. Quotech’s Big Story Case studies. Quotech works with MGAs, insurers, and brokers large and small to deliver the efficiencies which leading-edge, custom-crafted insurance technology can create. These case studies delve into just some of those success stories. Guillaume Bonnissent CEO Guillaume Bonnissent is Quotech’s founder and CEO. He’s also an underwriter with more than two decades’ experience, first at Euler, then at Hiscox for 15 years, then for four years as Underwriting Director at the MGA White Oak. In that last job he wanted to buy-in a decent underwriting platform, but couldn’t find a supplier who understood what an underwriter really needs, day to day. But he had learned some coding at college, so he built a platform himself to do the job, sold it, launched Quotech, and the rest is history. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to understand insurance business processes and the sector’s complex value chain like a native, then build systems which remove the inherent inefficiencies, not through chuck-it-all-out-and-start again approach, but incrementally. Follow Follow Marco Seoane Senior Software Developer Marco Seoane is Quotech’s front-end man, a Senior Software Developer with five years in the game, most of it with RecTech and MarTech early-stage B2B SaaS companies (before he found his home in insurTech, obviously). Marco says the best part about working in tech is that jeans and a t-shirt are acceptable workplace attire, but then his office is anywhere in London with an internet connection and a decent coffee. Give him those two, and he’ll get busy building and creating. “Idle hands are the devil’s workshop,” Marco says, as he pushes towards his self-imposed Friday production. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is all about reducing the cost of recording, managing, aggregating, and communicating about data, both cognitively and operationally. Follow Follow Lee John Martin Senior Software Developer Lee John Martin is Quotech’s main backend engineer (but claims “enough infrastructure and frontend knowledge to get myself into trouble”). A former graphic designer, he worked in insurTech for a year before joining Quotech, but during nearly a decade developing has built a geospatial SaaS tool in the property sector, an order-processing tool for a major consumer products supplier, and contract management software for the engineering sector, among many others. A man who prefers marathon running to commuting (he’s done 10 big jogs, last count), Lee delivers for Quotech customers from a box-room in his home in Gloucestershire with a black cat called Bobs (short for Bobbie, short for Roberta). Lee says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to get in your user’s head. You have to understand the user’s problem to solve it properly. And, he says, smart, simple ways of solving people’s problems are usually doable, and go well beyond what they think is possible. Follow Follow Niall Grant Senior Software Engineer Niall Grant is Senior Software Engineer at Quotech. His specialist areas are early-stage product development, backend APIs, command-line interfaces, databases, and system integrations – all of which means he has very particular skills. He’s deployed them over 18 years to build tools for sectors including HR, cloud operations, consulting, gambling, enterprise sales, and coaching. Every project is fuelled by his love of making stuff that has a meaningful, positive impact on the working lives of others – which is just what we like to do at Quotech. He does all this from his office in Edinburgh, where, for a different kind of positive impact, he’s a volunteer helmsman on the Lifeboats. In all this he is observed by his Working Cocker Spaniel, Flo, who Niall attests “has never worked a day in her life.” Niall says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to understand the challenges clients face, then build the right abstractions to enable business process flexibility, surface useful data and information to inform decision makers, and get new features to market quickly. Follow Follow Chris Pickford Product Manager Chris Pickford is Quotech’s Product Manager. He moved here to insurTech after eight years spent testing critical systems developed for accountancy. Eastbourne is his home by the sea, where he and Maisie, his Staffie, go where the connection is best to ensure everything works as it should for Quotech clients. “Being a start-up allows us to focus on any issues we face quickly and efficiently,” Chris says, “which helps us find the best way to work, and lets us create amazing solutions to any issues our clients face.” He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is building insurTech software that’s intuitive for users, and creating easier ways of working to make sure the major pain points no longer exist. Follow Follow Daniel Loader Lead Platform Engineer Daniel Loader is Quotech’s Lead Platform Engineer. He’s spent nearly a decade honing his craft in diverse sectors stretching from groceries to cyber security, working for household names like Iceland and Nominet. Now he’s made the crossing to insurance. From his home office in Manchester he works his magic for Quotech clients, with limited support from his cat Piggy and his tortoise González. His goal: to enable software engineers and ultimate users to work faster, with greater reliability, in part by deploying adjacent technology disciplines that provide the platform and services they need to succeed. Daniel says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to minimise users’ manual toil by making the workflow intuitive and the functionality smooth. Follow Follow Will Hunt Software Developer Will Hunt loves creative problem-solving. It’s the perfect predilection for a Quotech Software Developer. He does it in Go (the computer language), a skill he’s been perfecting over 11 years as a programmer, latterly for Sky. The best bit, he says, is the payoff: seeing something he’s built work better for users than they ever expected, making life easier for them. When he’s not coding from his front room in Plymouth, flanked by dogs Link and Apollo, cats Pixel and Artemis, a corn snake called Loki and a small sea’s worth of fish, Will is gaming or writing a science-fantasy novel. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to get feedback regularly from clients and users, measuring their requirements against your work. “You can’t get it right working in a vacuum,” he says. Follow Ezequiel Lopes Software Developer Ezequiel Lopes is an Argentinian from Bournemouth who studied CompSci in Portsmouth but grew up in Italy. We’re delighted he’s settled as a Software Developer at Quotech, where the positivity he brings to the team is as valuable as his intuitions as a front-end developer. He believes the best software comes from strong communication and shared understanding. A near-evangelical tech believer, he’s driven by the desire to simplify or automate to save precious time. Any he recoups for himself he spends playing basketball, Latin dancing, or adding to his list of 20 countries visited. He says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to understand the end user’s specific needs, make it intuitive and easy to use, and future-proof the app with scalability and flexibility. Follow Follow Ellen Daly Software Engineer Ellen Daly claims to be a life-long nerd at heart, so she fits right in as a Quotech Software Developer. Ellen loves problem-solving, and building things that help make people’s lives easier. She began her tech career as a UX researcher after a stint an academic researcher, then made the switch to development about two years ago. She’s never been happier in her work than now, she says! From her home office in a quiet Yorkshire village (complete with woodland view and golden retriever insatiable for belly rubs), Ellen works happily across the front- and back-ends, since that lets her get hands-on with the full picture. Ellen says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance – and what Quotech is really good at – is bridging the gap between what users need and what gets built. (That’s where, in former jobs, she’s seen many apps fall short.) The solution, she says, is to understand users deeply, and shape your solutions with them at the forefront. Follow Follow Esme Knight Software Developer Birmingham-based Esme Knight is a recreational climber who spends days surmounting challenges as a Quotech Software Developer. She’s perfect for the job, since she likes to get stuck into a problem. Give Esme a brief, and she will work out the detail of what’s needed from her very broad perspective: she injects working experience garnered over years in tech for automotive dealerships and in the TV, film, and theatre space. (Who wouldn’t give that up for insurance?) She loves the tech biz because every day’s a school day, but she keeps the arts close to her heart. Esme says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is the same as it is for any other industry: know the domain, which means you’re forced to keep asking questions. Esme’s questions come from a desk wedged into a corner of her living room. Follow Follow Rosa Catena Associate Product Manager Rosa Catena , Associate Product Manager at Quotech, lives in Staffordshire under the shadow of Alton Towers. With nearly a decade of tech experience under her belt, she switched to insurance from creating online buying journeys for the automotive industry. She’s an Italian on paper, but raised in Switzerland, and somehow has French as her strongest language (second to English). Her office is anywhere with strong Wi-Fi and strong coffee, and hopefully a dog (she has a crazy border collie called Luna). She likes Quotech because she can make positive, crucial changes, and is able to speak her mind in a shop that’s small enough for everyone’s voice to matter, but serious enough about the problem that the work feels real. Rosa says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is trust. It is essential to instil trust in end-users, she says, to make their journey seamless. Follow Follow Tanith Rietti Lead Quality Assurance Engineer Tanith Rietti is Quotech’s Quality Assurance Specialist, which is a polite way of saying she’s paid to break things before clients can. With more than 15 years in technology behind her, she has a knack for finding the one path through an application that nobody thought to test. She has a conviction that the fast pace and constant problem-solving of her work are exactly what make it worth doing (and who could argue?). Before she found her way into technology for insurance, Tanith sharpened her instincts across e-commerce and the jewellery trade, two worlds where the details really do matter. Meanwhile Tanith is a committed advocate for women in tech and for neurodiversity, and brings her spirit of championing others to the team. Tanith says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is simple to state but hard to achieve: understand the users and the industry, and everything else follows. At Quotech, the friendly, collaborative, and “genuinely in it together” culture make that easier, she says. Follow Follow Alex Mills Senior Platform Engineer Alex Mills , Senior Platform Engineer at Quotech, has worked in technology for 17 years, but he still finds real satisfaction in taking something people dread to use and transforming it into something they don’t need to think about. To do that, he digs deep into problems, usually by asking “why” more times than is strictly comfortable. He came to insurance without the industry’s embedded assumptions, so he asks often. That turns out to matter more than you might think. He solves technology challenges from his home in Droitwich, which he describes as “somewhat over-engineered” due to his Wallace-like automation of things that absolutely did not need it. Plus, it’s a menagerie, shared with Moscow and Wilson (former racehorses), Shiny and Strawberry (goldfish), and Molly the cat. Remaining time is spent away from the screen with family (mostly, when he’s not playing D&D with childhood friends, or tracking aircraft). Alex says the secret to making a truly useful technology app for insurance is to build something that fits that workflow, rather than fights with it. The best software removes steps. It never adds a system that busy people have to feed. It also has to be transparent, because no one will stake a risk decision on a black box. Follow Follow Meet the team. Alongside quarterly team meetings, we are electronically connected to create a genuine culture of camaraderie and purpose that leaves a minimal environment footprint. We hire based entirely on merit, and reward employees with competitive pay, share options for all employees under the Quotech Enterprise Management Incentives scheme, and a comprehensive healthcare package. For those who prefer an out-of-home office, we provide access to a local shared facility, and equipment is supplied for all. We’re always looking for new talent.
